title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཐེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 179)
shelf_note: A Derge woodblock folio of verse-and-prose debate on pramāṇa (arbiters, infinite regress, valid cognition), consistent with the Tshad ma section.

ocr_errors.image: start of line 2 looks closer to ཀ་རྩོད་པ་ན། (གཉིས་ཀ་རྩོད་པ་ན, 'when both dispute'); low confidence at this resolution
ocr_errors.problem: possible misread of particles at the line seam; sense barely affected

tr_errors_A.english: the two means of realization <note>the arguments or perspectives of the two disputants</note> will conflict. If other means of realization are required...
tr_errors_A.problem: rtogs byed here are the arbiters/judges of the debate (people), not 'means of realization'; the note wrongly identifies them with the disputants' arguments, which obscures the argument (arbiters disagree → further arbiters → regress)

tr_errors_A.english: those who provide the means of realization—the proponent and the opponent—have differing intellects
tr_errors_A.problem: three parties (arbiters, proponent, respondent) collapsed into two; the arbiters are made identical with the disputants

tr_errors_A.english: it is only in a certain way that the previous claim is harmed by this
tr_errors_A.problem: agent and patient swapped: source says the prior claim harms this, not that it is harmed by this; 'gsang ste brjod' rendered 'secretly asked'

tr_errors_A.english: how can you speak of all desires being non-existent or incomplete?
tr_errors_A.problem: 'dod here is the intended/asserted (thesis), not 'desires'; misleading
Buddhas assert distinctions, not have differing intentions

tr_errors_B.english: in whatever manner a previous acceptance might be harmed by this, it is not harmed by what arrives through the force of valid cognition
tr_errors_B.problem: agent/patient muddled (prior claim harms this) and the sentence becomes self-contradictory, since 'this' is what arrives through valid cognition

tr_errors_B.english: Whoever holds the conceit of truth asserts that there is no objective referent.
tr_errors_B.problem: that toward which truth is presumed is held [by the author] to lack a referent; B makes the conceited person the one asserting it

tr_errors_B.english: defending Madhyamaka critiques of inherent truth
tr_errors_B.problem: school label in summary is an inference not stated on the page

pages.prefer_reason: B correctly renders rtogs byed as arbiters and keeps arbiters, proponent and respondent distinct, so the regress argument reads clearly, whereas A misidentifies the arbiters with the disputants (with a wrong gloss) and has more moderate slips.

book_verdict: A clean Derge pramāṇa folio with a good transcription; both translations are serviceable, B being the more faithful, with no serious errors in either.
